Round 2 — diagnosis first: last round's density batch was reverted wholesale, and I now understand why. The acceptance test is scoreAlign = hv*1e6 + hvd on the pre-compaction layout, and a batch that leaves hv flat while costing even one 45 is a net loss, so it is thrown away entirely. My round-1 pack traded away three diagonals (4-35, 45-36, 2-3) for pure density and hv never moved, so all twenty moves went back; only compactGridSafe's own 58x59 -> 27x27 survived. The lesson is that density has to be *paid for* with an hv gain in the same batch, and that is what this round does. Two real segments first: 4 slides east along its locked row 3 onto column 8, which is 35's column, so 4-35 becomes vertical (column 8 carries vertical edges only from row 7 up, so row 3 is clear); and 3 slides east along its locked row 0 onto column 18, which is 2's column, so 2-3 becomes vertical (column 18 is otherwise empty). That is hv 61 -> 63, which dominates the secondary key no matter what happens to the diagonals. Everything else is the density work re-run under that cover, and this time I checked each one against the 45s as well: 36 west to (13,15) loses the 36-23 diagonal but gains 45-36 at dx=dy=5, a wash; 0 to (12,9) stays on 20's anti-diagonal so the 45 is preserved while column 11 empties; 35 up to (8,6) stays on column 8 so the new vertical to 4 holds. The rest touch no diagonal at all and each slides a single-occupant band onto a neighbouring occupied one along an axis the vertex is already locked to: columns 2, 3, 6, 9, 10, 11, 14, 15, 19, 23, 25 and rows 1, 2, 4, 7, 8, 11, 17, 22, 24. Row 26 is the one I could not free — 52 must stay north of 49 or the winding at 49 flips, and row 26 is the only row north of it. Expected result: 63/74 H/V on a 16x18 grid.
